item.title: Celebrating King’s Lynn’s historic figures
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Celebrating King’s Lynn’s historic figures
King’s Lynn is home to three statues honouring figures who shaped both the town and the wider world. The collection includes a bronze tribute to King John on New Conduit Street, unveiled in 2016 to mark the monarch’s 1204 charter which granted the town its independence.
The town also features a statue of explorer Captain George Vancouver on Purfleet Quay, commemorating his extensive mapping of the Northwest Pacific coastline. Finally, a statue at Guanock Place celebrates Frederick Savage, a renowned engineer and former mayor who became famous for his pioneering work on steam-powered fairground rides. These landmarks serve as a permanent reminder of the town’s rich history and the significant contributions of these three men.

King’s Lynn man to face trial over Wisbech exposure charges
A 54-year-old man from King’s Lynn is set to stand trial following allegations of indecent exposure in Wisbech. Simon Wells, of Oak Avenue, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He faces charges relating to multiple incidents between June 1 and September 1 of this year, where he is accused of intentionally exposing himself to cause alarm or distress.
Mr. Wells entered a not guilty plea and has been released on conditional bail, which prohibits him from contacting the victim. The case has been adjourned, and he is due to return to the same court on January 14 for trial.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Waterstones names Book of the Week
Waterstones in King’s Lynn has selected ‘Craftland: A Journey Through Britain's Living Past’ by James Fox as its current Book of the Week. The publication explores the work of remaining master craftspeople across the country, ranging from wheelwrights to silversmiths. The author examines how traditional trades and vanishing skills have helped shape British national identity and regional culture over hundreds of years.
The store on Norfolk Street has also released its latest top ten list, which includes titles by authors such as Elly Griffiths, Anthony Horowitz, and Sarah Vaughan. Readers can find more information on these selections by visiting the King’s Lynn branch.

King’s Lynn care provider placed in special measures
A King’s Lynn-based home care service, Dedicated Care East Anglia, has been downgraded to "inadequate" by the Care Quality Commission. The watchdog found the provider breached five legal regulations, including those regarding safeguarding and safe care. Inspectors raised concerns over staff using faulty equipment and failing to follow care plans. One report noted a staff member left a distressed client to smoke outside.
The service, based at Tansley Business Park, is now in special measures and will be closely monitored. While the firm expressed disappointment and is challenging some findings, it has appointed external experts to review its processes. The CQC noted that some families reported feeling their relatives were treated with dignity and respect.

item.title: New NHS guidance changes ward access for Norfolk hospitals
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New NHS guidance changes ward access for Norfolk hospitals
Norfolk hospitals, including the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, are updating their policies following new guidance from NHS England. The rules require that single-sex hospital services, such as wards, toilets, and bathrooms, be provided based on a patient's biological sex rather than gender identity.
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group says it is reviewing the implications of the guidance to ensure compliance. The new policy, which also applies to mental health facilities and GP surgeries, includes exceptions for areas like A&E and critical care. Where biological sex placement is not clinically appropriate, hospitals are instructed to provide alternatives, such as single rooms. Trusts have been asked to implement these changes at pace.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/hospital-to-stop-allowing-trans-women-onto-female-wards-foll-9487339/

item.description:

Concerns raised over potential Queen Elizabeth Hospital service changes
Independent borough councillor Jo Rust has raised concerns regarding a strategic review of Norfolk’s three hospitals. A leaked report suggests potential plans to centralise Accident and Emergency services in Norwich and downgrade facilities at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn.
Senior doctors have warned that such changes could lead to a workforce crisis and increased distress for patients. The hospital’s chief executive, Lesley Dwyer, has cited changing healthcare needs and birth rates as reasons for reviewing maternity, ICU, and A&E services. A protest is planned for this Saturday at 11.30am at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn. Residents are being encouraged to share their views by emailing Healthwatch Norfolk.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk Council declines to detail swimming pool planning costs
West Norfolk Council has declined a request to provide a breakdown of the £845,609 spent on planning a new swimming pool at Lynnsport. The local authority stated that the information is commercially sensitive and that releasing details could prejudice future contract negotiations.
The proposed £23 million facility is intended to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool. Council leader Alistair Beales defended the expenditure, noting that planning in a flood zone involves uncertain ground conditions. While the council approved the planning budget last month, officials emphasised that the project remains in the development phase. Previous attempts to relocate the pool to Lynnsport were abandoned after feasibility studies suggested costs could exceed £45 million.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/council-refuses-to-share-cost-breakdown-of-850k-spend-for-p-9487073/
